title: SRT3 Network
description: Internet health, hop-by-hop latency, the 10G fabric, every physical NIC, router, and service checks.

panels.title: Ping, hop by hop
panels.description: Hellcat -> router -> AT&T gateway -> internet. Whichever hop jumps first is where the problem is.

panels.title: Cloudflare ping distribution
panels.description: Each column is a time slice; brighter cells = more pings at that latency. A tight bright band = a stable line. Smears upward = jitter.

panels.title: Packet loss (5 min rolling)
panels.description: Share of pings with no reply. Ryzenous shows loss while asleep - expected.

panels.title: DNS lookup time
panels.description: Time to resolve google.com via the router and via Cloudflare directly. If the router is much slower, its DNS is the bottleneck.

panels.title: 10G traffic per host
panels.description: rx+tx on each 10 Gbit/s NIC. iperf3 peaked at 9.91 Gbit/s - that's the ceiling.

panels.title: 10G fabric ping
panels.description: Hellcat to the other nodes over 10G vs over the 1G LAN. 10G should be lower and flatter.

panels.title: 10G live (every scrape, for benchmarks)
panels.description: Raw per-scrape rate (15 s steps), not the 1-minute average above, so short iperf3 phases show at full height.

panels.title: Last iperf3 run (Viper - Demon)
panels.description: push = Viper to Demon, pull = Demon to Viper, bidir = both at once (max 20). Rerun on Viper: systemd-run --unit=srt3-iperf --collect /root/srt3-iperf.sh

panels.title: Retransmits (last run)
panels.description: TCP resends during each 45 s phase. Hundreds to a few thousand at 10G is normal; tens of thousands means a bad cable, optic or NIC.

panels.title: Last benchmark
panels.description: When the last iperf3 run finished.

panels.title: $node: traffic per NIC (in up, out down)
panels.description: This row repeats once per host selected in the Hosts dropdown.

panels.title: $node: link utilization
panels.description: Busier direction / negotiated link speed.

panels.title: $node: errors + drops
panels.description: Should be flat zero. Anything else = bad cable, MTU mismatch, or a struggling driver.

panels.title: Link speed, MTU, utilization
panels.description: Every physical NIC. 10G ports should show 10 Gb/s and MTU 9000; if not, an alert fires.

panels.title: Router - GL.iNet Flint 2  (needs the optional router step)
Router traffic per interface (in up, out down)
panels.description: WAN = the port to the AT&T gateway. Empty until prometheus-node-exporter-lua is installed on the router.

panels.title: Router conntrack entries
panels.description: Open NAT connections through the router.

panels.title: Queries (24h)
panels.description: DNS lookups from every device in AdGuard's 24h window.

panels.title: Blocked (24h)
panels.description: Ads, trackers, malware.

panels.title: Malware blocked
panels.description: Safe-browsing hits: a device tried a known-bad domain.

panels.title: Avg lookup time
panels.description: AdGuard's average processing time per query.

panels.title: Protection
panels.description: Filtering on/off. 'down' = Hellcat can't reach the AdGuard API.

panels.title: Blocked % over time
panels.description: Rolling 24h block rate. A sudden jump can mean a device started phoning home a lot.

panels.title: Queries in the latest hour
panels.description: AdGuard's current hourly bucket.

panels.title: Top clients (24h)
panels.description: Which devices make the most DNS lookups. IoT devices showing up high here are worth a look.

panels.title: Response time per service
panels.description: Full HTTP round-trip from Hellcat, every 30s.

panels.title: Service checks
panels.description: Status, HTTP code, and days until the TLS cert expires (Proxmox self-signed certs last ~2 years).
